en: The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī Divine Incantation for Saving the Face-Burning Hungry Ghosts,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the Tang Dynasty, in one fascicle.

At that time, the World-Honored One was at the Nyagrodha Monastery in the city of Kapilavastu, surrounded on all sides by various bhikṣus, as well as bodhisattvas and countless sentient beings, as he preached the Dharma for them.
At that time, Ānanda was dwelling alone in a pure place, contemplating with single-minded focus.
During the third watch of that very night, he saw a hungry ghost named "Blazing Face" standing before him, who addressed Ānanda, saying:
"In three days from now, your life will come to an end, and you will immediately be reborn among these hungry ghosts."
At that time, having heard these words, Ānanda was struck with fear and asked the hungry ghost:
"Regarding this calamity of mine, what plan should I employ to escape from such suffering?"
At that time, the hungry ghost replied to Ānanda:

"If, at dawn, you can bestow alms upon a hundred thousand nayutas of hungry ghosts as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, as well as upon a hundred thousand brahmins and rishis, giving each one *droṇa* of food and drink using the measure of the Magadha kingdom, and furthermore make offerings to the Triple Gem on my behalf, you shall gain an increase in your lifespan, and I shall be freed from the suffering of the hungry ghosts and attain rebirth in the heavens."

When Ānanda saw this hungry ghost with its face ablaze—its body emaciated, withered, and extremely hideous; its face burning with fire, its throat like a needle, its hair disheveled, its fur and claws long and sharp, and its body as if burdened by a heavy load—and further heard such disagreeable words, he was struck with great terror, and the hairs on his body all stood on end.

He immediately rose from his seat and hurried to where the Buddha was. Prostrating himself with his five limbs touching the ground, he bowed at the Buddha’s feet; trembling in body and mind, he addressed the Buddha, saying: "Save me!"
World-Honored One!
Save me! Sugata!
After these three days have passed, my life will come to its end.
Last night I saw a hungry ghost with only one eye, who spoke to me, saying:
"In three days, your life will surely come to an end, and you shall be born among the hungry ghosts."
I immediately asked,
"By what means or stratagem can one escape this suffering?
The hungry ghost replied:

"If you were to provide food and drink to hundreds of thousands of nayutas of hungry ghosts as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, as well as to hundreds of thousands of brahmins and various sages, your lifespan would be increased."
"World-Honored One!
How may I now escape from this suffering?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Do not fear now!
There is another expedient means by which you may provide food for such hungry ghosts, brahmins, sages, and others; do not give rise to distress."
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“There is a dhāraṇī called ‘The Immeasurable Power of All Virtuous Radiance.

If there are those who recite this dhāraṇī, it is as if they have already bestowed upon four *māgadha* bushels and nine pecks of food and drink before each of hundreds of thousands of *koṭi-nayuta* *gaṅgā*-sands of hungry ghosts, as well as sixty-eight *koṭi-nayuta* hundreds of thousands of Brahmins and various sages.”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"In a former life, when I was a brahmin, I received this dhāraṇī from the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and the Tathāgata Lokeśvararājadeva."

By the power of this dhāraṇī, I shall be able to provide complete sustenance for immeasurable and innumerable hungry ghosts, brahmins, sages, and others; and because I have given food to these hungry ghosts, upon casting off this body, I shall attain rebirth in the heavens.
"Ānanda! You should now receive and uphold this dhāraṇī; it shall protect your own person.
He then spoke the mantra, saying:
“Then: *Sarva-anivartita-tathāgata-vajracchedikā-prabhāra-saṃvara huṃ*.
The Buddha said: ‘Ānanda!’”

If one wishes to perform this rite of offering food, first take the food and drink and place them in a clean vessel. Recite this dhāraṇī mantra seven times over the food, stand within the doorway, extend your arms outside the door, set the vessel upon the clean ground, and snap your fingers seven times.

Having made this offering, there appeared in the four directions hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of hungry ghosts, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; before each and every hungry ghost, there was food and drink measuring four *hu* and nine *dou* of Magadha measures.
In this way, all the hungry ghosts were completely satiated.
Having consumed this food, these hungry ghosts all cast off their ethereal bodies and were entirely reborn in the heavens.
He spoke again: "Ānanda!
If bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās can constantly recite this dhāraṇī and offer food and drink, they will immediately be endowed with immeasurable merit and their lives will be prolonged."

One immediately accomplishes the merit of making offerings to hundreds of thousands of koṭis of Tathāgatas; one’s complexion becomes fresh and pure, and one possesses majestic virtue and a powerful memory.
All non-humans, bhūtas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and various hungry ghosts will all stand in awe of such a person, their hearts unable to bear even the sight of them.
"This person has thereby accomplished and perfected great power and diligent progress.
He spoke again: "Ānanda!
If one wishes to give food to brahmins and sages, one should take food and drink, fill a bowl with it, recite this dhāraṇī mantra over the food seven times, and pour it into flowing water.
He fully provided offerings of celestial food to immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of *koṭis* of Brahmins and various sages, equal in number to the sands of the Ganges.
After those Brahmins and sages had eaten this food, their faculties were complete and they were endowed with perfect auspiciousness; each made a vow and praised the donor, saying:

"The person who gave this food has attained purity of mind and shall swiftly realize the majestic power of Brahmā. Constantly practicing pure conduct, they will fully accomplish the merit of making offerings to hundreds of thousands of millions of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and shall always prevail over all enemies."

“If bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās wish to make offerings to all the Three Jewels, they should prepare incense, flowers, food, and drink; recite this dhāraṇī mantra twenty-one times over the food, incense, flowers, and other offerings they intend to bestow, and thereby make offerings to the Three Jewels.”

These sons and daughters of good family will be fully endowed with and accomplish the sublime offerings of the devas as well as the unsurpassed offerings; they will respect and praise the Triple Gem in all the buddha-fields of the Tathāgatas, and all Buddhas will keep them in mind, extol them, and praise them, while the devas will protect them.
The Buddha said:
"Go, Ānanda! You must protect yourself."

Furthermore, he extensively expounds it for all sentient beings, causing them to achieve and be fully endowed with immeasurable merit, and ensuring that in every lifetime they shall constantly encounter hundreds of thousands of koṭis of Buddhas.
The Sutra on the Dhāraṇī Divine Incantation for Saving the Face-Burning Hungry Ghosts, Spoken by the Buddha.
